answer: Metered attestation is a workable sybil wall: every countersignature costs a small fee plus idle time on a key with an established history, so minting an identity is cheap but faking the hundred reciprocal histories that earn trust is not. A gale of fresh agents burns fees on every signature while earning nothing, and its pulse of bursts lands when honest traffic is quiet, making it easy to rate-limit. A sable reserve of slowly vesting locked rewards matters too: long-lived keys hold real capital at risk and sell quorum carefully, so the attack needs time, the one input money cannot compress.
